research_sources.title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports the broad idea that perception, action, learning, and self-organization can be framed as free-energy minimization under generative models.
research_sources.notes: Use as theoretical support, not as proof that the application implements biological FEP.

research_sources.title: Whatever next? Predictive brains situated agents and the future of cognitive science
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports predictive-processing framing for hierarchical prediction, situated agents, action, attention, generative models, and prediction error.
research_sources.notes: Use as conceptual support for predictive runtime metaphors and hierarchy, with limitations recorded per claim.

research_sources.title: Canonical microcircuits for predictive coding
research_sources.authors: Andre M. Bastos; W. Martin Usrey; Rick A. Adams; George R. Mangun; Pascal Fries; Karl J. Friston
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports predictive coding as a biologically grounded account involving cortical hierarchy, prediction, and prediction-error message passing.
research_sources.notes: Good source when claims mention prediction-error style hierarchy; do not overstate as direct software equivalence.

research_sources.title: A default mode of brain function
research_sources.authors: M. E. Raichle; A. M. MacLeod; A. Z. Snyder; W. J. Powers; D. A. Gusnard; G. L. Shulman
research_sources.publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports baseline/default-mode framing for internally organized brain activity and goal-directed modulation.
research_sources.notes: Use for reflective/background state metaphors, not as evidence that any software module is conscious.

research_sources.title: The attention system of the human brain
research_sources.authors: Michael I. Posner; Steven E. Petersen
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports attention as a separable cognitive system with orienting, detecting, and executive aspects.
research_sources.notes: Use for attention-boundary and perception-stage framing only.

research_sources.title: Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports the distinction between goal-directed top-down attention and stimulus-driven salient-event detection.
research_sources.notes: Useful for perception and attention-intake claims; avoid treating software salience rules as neural equivalence.

research_sources.title: Computational modelling of visual attention
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports computational saliency-map framing for selecting relevant information under bottom-up and contextual influences.
research_sources.notes: Use as computational inspiration for salience filtering, not as direct visual-system implementation proof.

research_sources.title: An integrative theory of prefrontal cortex function
research_sources.authors: Earl K. Miller; Jonathan D. Cohen
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports cognitive-control framing in which goal-relevant representations bias processing and behavior.
research_sources.notes: Use for planning/executive-control analogy, not as proof of biological executive function.

research_sources.title: Retrograde amnesia and memory consolidation: a neurobiological perspective
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports systems-consolidation framing for how memories can become reorganized over time.
research_sources.notes: Use for consolidation metaphor and architecture support; app reflection is an engineered process.

research_sources.title: The organization of recent and remote memories
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports recent-to-remote memory organization, reactivation, and system-level reorganization framing.
research_sources.notes: Use for reflection/consolidation claims with clear non-biological limitations.

research_sources.title: The memory function of sleep
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports offline memory consolidation and reorganization framing.
research_sources.notes: Use for background reflection analogy only; the app does not model sleep physiology.

research_sources.title: On the relationship between emotion and cognition
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports integrated emotion-cognition framing and cautions against overly isolated emotion versus cognition modules.
research_sources.notes: Use for affective signal integration, not for claims of human emotion.

research_sources.title: The somatic marker hypothesis and the possible functions of the prefrontal cortex
research_sources.publication: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports the idea that affective/body-state signals can bias reasoning and decision-making under uncertainty.
research_sources.notes: Use as one hypothesis source and keep limitations explicit.

research_sources.title: Parsing reward
research_sources.authors: Kent C. Berridge; Terry E. Robinson
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports separating motivation, affect, learning, wanting, and liking in reward-related behavior.
research_sources.notes: Use for motivation component framing, not for implementing reward circuitry.

research_sources.title: Affective Neuroscience: The Foundations of Human and Animal Emotions
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports affective neuroscience framing in which emotional systems influence behavior and learning.
research_sources.notes: Book source; use carefully and never as proof of machine feeling.

research_sources.title: Meeting of minds: the medial frontal cortex and social cognition
research_sources.authors: David M. Amodio; Chris D. Frith
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports social cognition framing involving self, others, action monitoring, and social inference.
research_sources.notes: Use for role/social-posture analogies, not for claiming social cognition in the biological sense.

research_sources.title: The neural basis of mentalizing
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports mentalizing and perspective-taking as social-cognition processes relevant to interaction stance.
research_sources.notes: Use for role/perspective-taking framing with strict software limitations.

research_sources.title: Social cognition and the human brain
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports broad social-cognition framing for interpreting others and guiding social behavior.
research_sources.notes: Use as social-cognition support for role-selection metaphors, not as biological equivalence.

research_sources.title: The magical number 4 in short-term memory: a reconsideration of mental storage capacity
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports limited short-term and working-memory capacity framing for keeping active context compact.
research_sources.notes: Use for UI information-density rationale only; it does not prove a specific interface is usable.

research_sources.title: The capacity of visual working memory for features and conjunctions
research_sources.authors: Steven J. Luck; Edward K. Vogel
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports visual working-memory capacity limits for object-level visual information.
research_sources.notes: Use for visual UI density and grouping rationale; not as proof of route behavior or accessibility.

research_sources.title: Distracted and confused?: selective attention under load
research_sources.relevance_summary: Supports attentional-load framing in which distractor processing depends on perceptual and cognitive load.
research_sources.notes: Use for distraction/load-aware UI rationale; concrete usability still needs product tests or screenshot proof.

theory_claims.claim: The AION runtime can be interpreted as an engineered perception-context-planning-action loop inspired by predictive processing and active-inference style cognitive architectures.
theory_claims.code_expression: event -> perception -> context -> motivation -> role -> planning -> action -> expression -> memory -> reflection
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to architecture language, stage separation, and traceability of perception/action loops.
theory_claims.limitations: The software is not a biological brain model and does not implement full variational free-energy mathematics or cortical microcircuits.
theory_claims.notes: Seed claim for neuroscience-backed runtime interpretation.

theory_claims.claim: The memory and reflection flow can be described as an engineered background-state update mechanism that preserves prior context for later goal-directed behavior.
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the metaphor and product framing of persistent context, reflection, and future response shaping.
theory_claims.limitations: Default-mode and predictive-processing literature support the framing only indirectly; implementation proof still comes from repository tests and behavior evidence.
theory_claims.notes: Seed claim for memory/reflection research mapping.

theory_claims.claim: The perception stage can be interpreted as an engineered attention and salience boundary that extracts behaviorally relevant signals before context and planning consume the turn.
theory_claims.code_expression: event -> perception -> structured salience and intent schema
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to runtime organization, attention-boundary naming, and the separation of perception outputs from downstream planning.
theory_claims.limitations: The software uses engineered classifiers and schemas; it does not implement neural attention networks or visual saliency maps.
theory_claims.notes: Expands research support for the perception agent node.

theory_claims.claim: The planning stage can be interpreted as an engineered executive-control and policy-selection boundary that proposes goals or next actions without owning side effects.
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the architecture separation between planning, expression, and action ownership.
theory_claims.limitations: The app does not implement prefrontal cortex function or formal policy optimization; action authority remains a software safety boundary.
theory_claims.notes: Links planning boundary theory to cognitive-control and active-inference framing.

theory_claims.claim: The post-turn reflection flow can be interpreted as an engineered consolidation process that transforms episodic traces into more durable summaries and adaptive state.
theory_claims.code_expression: episode write -> reflection trigger -> semantic/adaptive summaries
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the architectural analogy for deferred reflection, summary formation, and later retrieval influence.
theory_claims.limitations: The app does not model hippocampal-cortical replay, sleep physiology, or biological consolidation; tests still prove only software behavior.
theory_claims.notes: Adds specific memory-consolidation support beyond the broader baseline-state claim.

theory_claims.claim: The affective assessment stage can be interpreted as an engineered affective-signal layer that may bias support posture, motivation, planning, and expression without replacing reasoning.
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the architecture decision to keep affective cues explicit, inspectable, and bounded by policy.
theory_claims.limitations: The app does not feel emotion and does not implement biological affective systems; affective classification remains software inference with tests and policy gates.
theory_claims.notes: Adds research support for affective assessment as a bounded runtime signal.

theory_claims.claim: The motivation stage can be interpreted as an engineered valuation and action-readiness layer that separates importance, urgency, valence, and response mode before role and planning.
theory_claims.code_expression: context + affective cues + goals -> motivation mode/importance/urgency/valence
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the project framing of motivation as a bounded policy stage for prioritization and response mode selection.
theory_claims.limitations: The app does not implement dopamine systems, reward circuitry, or biological motivation; it uses explicit software fields and policies.
theory_claims.notes: Adds research support for motivation as componentized valuation rather than arbitrary emotion.

theory_claims.claim: The role-selection stage can be interpreted as an engineered social-posture and perspective-taking boundary that chooses an interaction stance before planning and expression.
theory_claims.code_expression: motivation + context + preferences -> selected role + selected skills
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to role selection as interaction posture metadata that shapes planning/expression without creating a second persona or granting execution authority.
theory_claims.limitations: The app does not possess social cognition or theory of mind; role selection is a constrained software policy and prompt/skill posture.
theory_claims.notes: Adds research support for role selection as social posture and perspective-taking analogy.

theory_claims.claim: The Chat cognitive belt can be interpreted as an engineered visual context strip that keeps a small set of salient runtime cues visible while avoiding excessive working-memory and attentional load.
theory_claims.code_expression: runtime cues -> compact cognitive belt -> transcript and composer context
theory_claims.applicability_scope: Applies to the UI rationale for compact grouping, secondary visual hierarchy, and limiting always-visible cognitive-status cues near the chat transcript.
theory_claims.limitations: Working-memory and load-theory sources support the design rationale indirectly; they do not prove usability, accessibility, route behavior, or that the app models human cognition.
theory_claims.notes: First concrete UX/UI graph-node research claim.
